_readme: SS-201. Commits listed here are ignored when working out the newest commit that
touched a source file. They are the commits that changed every file without changing
This list exists because the freshness rule is otherwise unusable. A sitewide
accessibility or footer pass resets the git date on every page at once, and a rule
keyed to raw git dates then reports 26 content changes that did not happen -- which
trains you to ignore it, which is worse than not having it.
Add a SHA here only when the commit genuinely changed no page content. If it touched
copy on even one page, do not exclude it; fix that page's lastmod instead.

exclusions.reason: Bulk non-content rewrite: added a <main> landmark to every page and stopped footer links relying on colour alone. Touched all 32 HTML files, changed no published copy, and reset every git date to 2026-08-20.

Added the calendly_open and contact_submit GA4 events to index.html, contact.html and prophet-21.html. Script blocks only -- no published copy changed on any of the three pages, so their sitemap lastmod should not move and tell search engines otherwise.
Added the calendly_booked GA4 event to index.html, contact.html and prophet-21.html. One script block per page, no published copy changed, so their sitemap lastmod should not move.

Phase 5 CSS consolidation. Replaced the inline <style> block on 22 pages with links to /assets/site.<hash>.css plus doc.<hash>.css or article.<hash>.css. Every rule was carried across unchanged and an equivalence pass compared the effective value of every declaration on every page before and after -- see docs/css-consolidation-2026-08-26.md. The only intended difference is --blue-bright defined once in :root instead of inlined as a var() fallback, which is the same colour. NO PUBLISHED COPY CHANGED on any of the 22, so their sitemap lastmod must not move and tell search engines otherwise.

Phase 6 typography. Self-hosted Inter, Playfair Display and JetBrains Mono, removed the fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com references from the two AI pages, and pointed 27 pages at the shared stacks. This CHANGES HOW PAGES LOOK and changes nothing any page says -- not a word of copy moved. A sitemap lastmod tells a search engine the content was revised, and it was not. The one thing here that is a disclosure change rather than a presentation change, the removal of a third party, is recorded in /corrections instead, which is where a reader would look for it.
